name: Bilhan
overview: Bilhan was a male Edomite, identified specifically as the son of Ezer. His mention in Scripture is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional notes or details about his life or character provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Bilhan means 'foolish' in Hebrew. This is the only recorded name for him, and it was not given by God. The meaning of his name is noted in Genesis 36:27 without further elaboration.
familyAndRelationships: Bilhan is explicitly recorded as the son of Ezer, establishing his place within the Edomite lineage. Beyond this father-son relationship, Scripture does not provide additional family connections for Bilhan.
scriptureSignificance: Bilhan's significance lies in his role within the genealogical record of the Edomites, as recorded in Genesis 36:27. His mention helps trace the lineage and tribal affiliations descending from Esau through Edom, contributing to the biblical understanding of God's providential unfolding of nations. While no further narrative details are given, his inclusion underscores the importance of preserving family lines in Scripture.
